subject: Post-call: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Li <samuel.li@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) - next steps

Hi Samuel / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — good alignment across product fit and usage patterns. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can map the right commercial path: 

Recap: 
- Pilot: ~2k inference hours / month expected, initial eval running for 3 months.
- Primary requirements: data isolation, audit logs, SLA for latency for customer-facing features.
- AP constraint: you mentioned internal PO process and vendor onboarding forms.

Questions / next steps we discussed: 
1) Payment method: do you expect to pay by corporate credit card or via a Purchase Order (PO) / net terms? Any internal thresholds (e.g., purchase size above which AP requires PO)?
2) Vendor onboarding: can you share the vendor onboarding form now (we can pre-fill Redwood’s details) and any required documents (W-9, COI/insurance)?
3) Marketplace interest: one alternative is purchasing via AWS Marketplace (shorter procurement path but has marketplace fees). Would procurement prefer that option?

Attachment: I’ve attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft-Redwood-v1.pdf) to speed contract discussions. I can also draft a concise MOU if that helps procurement routing.

Suggested mutual action plan (high level):
- You: confirm PO vs card and share vendor onboarding form (Procurement) — target: EOM.
- Us: provide W-9, insurance cert, final SOW and vendor info; loop in Contracts if PO path chosen.
- Optional: If Marketplace is preferred, we’ll provide Marketplace order guide and pricing delta.

If it helps, I can loop Jordan (sales manager) and Aditya (solutions engineer) into the thread for contract/technical sign-off. What’s your preferred path?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment: SOW-draft-Redwood-v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Samuel Li <samuel.li@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) - next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — that matches our conversation. A few clarifications from AP: 

- AP policy: For any vendor spend > $25,000/year we require a formal PO and completed vendor onboarding (standard forms + W-9 + COI). For smaller pilots we can sometimes do a P-card/credit card.
- Vendor onboarding: I’ve attached Acme’s vendor onboarding form (acme_vendor_onboarding_form_filled.pdf) — we usually need the vendor to complete the sections for banking/contact/insurance and return with W-9 and COI.
- Marketplace: Procurement is open to Marketplace purchases if the vendor supports it, though we need confirmation on terms parity and any marketplace uplift. Marketplace is attractive because approvals and billing get simplified.

Timing: Procurement team is aiming to complete onboarding and issue a PO by the end of the month, assuming we have the required docs.

I’ll loop in the procurement coordinator (procurement@acme.com) for the formal steps.

Best,
Samuel Li
Senior PM, Platform Integrations | Acme Corp
samuel.li@acme.com

Attachment: acme_vendor_onboarding_form_filled.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Li <samuel.li@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) - next steps

Samuel — appreciate the quick turnaround and the filled form. Good to know the $25k threshold. A few notes / options to make this smoother: 

Option A — PO path (recommended for long-term contract / >$25k/year):
- We’ll return a completed vendor onboarding packet (W-9 + COI + vendor questionnaire).
- Redwood Legal can execute a short SOW + signature (DocuSign) and then your AP team issues a PO referencing the SOW.
- Timeline: contract + PO typically takes 2–4 weeks once we have all docs.

Option B — Credit card / P-card or Marketplace (fastest for pilot):
- If Procurement can approve card payments for pilot spend, you can be live in 1–2 business days.
- AWS Marketplace: we’re listed on AWS Marketplace (standardized terms). Marketplace purchases often bypass vendor onboarding but do carry a 7–12% marketplace fee. If Procurement prefers this, we can provide the marketplace ordering guide and estimated net cost.

Must-haves from our side (we’ll provide immediately): 
- W-9 (attached in this reply)
- Certificate of insurance (COI) — I’ll request from our ops team and share within 24 hours.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Confirm preferred payment path (PO vs card vs marketplace).
2) If PO: I’ll return completed vendor packet and Jordan will own contract cadence to get SOW signed via DocuSign.
3) If card/marketplace: we’ll send marketplace docs and confirm any pricing delta.

I’ve attached our W-9 and the SOW draft again for convenience. I’ll also loop Aditya on any technical questions you want included in the SOW.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: W-9-Redwood.pdf (PDF, 30KB), SOW-draft-Redwood-v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)
